interest: Indexes US intelligence on Japanese interest in Baja California naval bases and oil, iron, and scrap deals with Mexican elites.
overview: This file comprises pages 43 through 50 of the State Department's List of Papers (docket sheets) for decimal file 894.20212, recording entries 394 through 450 between February 1938 and November 1939 concerning Japanese military, naval, espionage, and economic activities in Mexico. The docket indexes incoming and outgoing communications, despatches, telegrams, and intelligence reports from U.S. consular posts across Mexico, the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City, the War and Navy Departments, the Department of Justice (FBI), and private citizens. Principal subjects include investigations into suspected Japanese naval base concessions and espionage along the Pacific coast and the Gulf of California, surveys and soundings around Puerto Libertad and Baja California, and alleged smuggling of Japanese nationals into the United States via fishing vessels based at Turtle Bay. In addition, the file heavily details Japanese efforts to capitalize on the 1938 Mexican oil expropriation by negotiating petroleum concessions, purchasing fuel oil through intermediaries, and inspecting the Poza Rica oil fields, as well as Japanese interest in iron ore deposits at Las Truchas, asbestos mines near Ensenada, salt concessions, and scrap iron exports.

subfiles.about: A docket register of State Department papers and cross-references regarding Japanese military, naval, espionage, petroleum, mining, and fishing activities in Mexico from 1938 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: This document comprises pages 43 through 50 of the State Department's List of Papers for decimal file 894.20212, recording entries 394 through 450 between February 1938 and November 1939. It systematically indexes correspondence, consular despatches, attaché reports, and inter-agency memoranda from the War Department, Navy Department, and FBI concerning Japanese espionage, soundings, and alleged naval base ambitions in Baja California and along the Pacific coast. The register also documents extensive intelligence regarding Japanese negotiations for Mexican oil contracts and concessions following expropriation, chartered flights to Poza Rica, and commercial interest in iron, salt, and scrap metal. Because the original communications were classified into other series such as 812.6363, 812.628, and 810.00, this List of Papers served as the department's central tracking record for Japanese activities in Mexico.
